title: 2016 年全国硕士研究生招生考试 英语（二）

sections.title: Section I　完形填空
sections.dir: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 主线：幸福地区企业投资与研发更多，因果未定但线索一致。7 题 Sure enough 是固定搭配。

paras.en: Happy people work differently. They're more productive, more creative, and willing to take greater risks. And new research suggests that happiness might influence 1 firms work, too.
paras.zh: 快乐的人工作方式不同。他们效率更高、更有创造力，也更愿意冒更大的风险。而新研究表明，幸福感或许也会影响企业如何运转。

paras.en: Companies located in places with happier people invest more, according to a recent research paper. 2 , firms in happy places spend more on R&D (research and development). That's because happiness is linked to the kind of longer-term thinking 3 for making investments for the future.
paras.zh: 据一份新近的研究论文，位于居民更快乐地区的企业投资更多。尤其是，位于快乐地区的企业在研发（研究与开发）上花得更多。这是因为幸福感与做长期投资所必需的那种长远思维相关。

paras.en: The researchers wanted to know if the 4 and inclination for risk-taking that come with happiness would 5 the way companies invested. So they compared U.S. cities' average happiness 6 by Gallup polling with the investment activity of publicly traded firms in those areas.
paras.zh: 研究者想知道，随幸福感而来的乐观心态与冒险倾向，是否会改变企业的投资方式。于是他们把盖洛普民调测得的美国各城市平均幸福度，与这些地区上市公司的投资活动作了比较。

paras.en: 7 enough, firms' investment and R&D intensity were correlated with the happiness of the area in which they were 8 . But is it really happiness that's linked to investment, or could something else about happier cities 9 why firms there spend more on R&D? To find out, the researchers controlled for various 10 that might make firms more likely to invest — like size, industry, and sales — and for indicators that a place was 11 to live in, like growth in wages or population. The link between happiness and investment generally 12 even after accounting for these things.
paras.zh: 果然，企业的投资与研发强度，与其总部所在地区的幸福度相关。但与投资相关的真的是幸福感吗？或者，快乐城市的其他某些特征，能否解释当地企业为何在研发上花得更多？为弄清这一点，研究者控制了可能让企业更愿意投资的各种因素——如规模、行业和销售额——也控制了某地宜居程度的指标，如工资或人口的增长。在考虑这些因素之后，幸福感与投资之间的关联总体上依然成立。

paras.en: The correlation between happiness and investment was particularly strong for younger firms, which the authors 13 to "less codified decision making process" and the possible presence of "younger and less 14 managers who are more likely to be influenced by sentiment." The relationship was 15 stronger in places where happiness was spread more 16 . Firms seem to invest more in places where most people are relatively happy, rather than in places with happiness inequality.
paras.zh: 幸福感与投资的关联在年轻企业中尤其明显。作者把这一点归因于“决策程序不够规范”，以及可能存在的“更年轻、经验更少、更容易受情绪影响的管理者”。在幸福感分布更均匀的地方，这种关系也更强。企业似乎更愿意在多数人相对快乐的地方投资，而不是在幸福感不均的地方投资。

paras.en: 17 this doesn't prove that happiness causes firms to invest more or to take a longer-term view, the authors believe it at least 18 at that possibility. It's not hard to imagine that local culture and sentiment would help 19 how executives think about the future. "It surely seems plausible that happy people would be more forward-thinking and creative and 20 R&D more than the average," said one researcher.
paras.zh: 虽然这并不能证明幸福感促使企业增加投资或着眼长远，但作者认为，它至少暗示了这种可能。不难想象，当地的文化与情绪会有助于塑造高管对未来的看法。一位研究者说：“快乐的人比普通人更有前瞻性、更有创造力，也更倾向于投入研发，这看来确实合情合理。”

items.exp: 定位首段末句 happiness might influence 1 firms work：宾语从句里 firms work 主谓齐全，缺的是方式状语，how 引出的正是“企业如何运转”。A 的 why 要接完整的原因句，语义变成“影响企业为何运转”，讲不通；where、when 与“工作方式”无关。
定位第二段②句：首句说快乐地区的企业投资更多，本句举出研发支出，属总分结构里的举例推进，In particular 意为“尤其、特别是”。A 的 In return 表回报，C 的 In contrast（原文作 convast）表对比，D 表总结，都无法承接这层“具体来说”。
定位同段末句 the kind of longer-term thinking 3 for making investments for the future：thinking 后接形容词短语作后置定语，“做长期投资所必需的长远思维”，necessary for 为固定搭配。D 的 sufficient for 虽也成立，但“足够”构不成“因为幸福”的理由，B、C 与投资语境不搭。
定位第三段首句 the 4 and inclination for risk-taking that come with happiness：空格与 inclination 并列，都被幸福感带来，optimism（乐观）与冒险倾向同属积极心态。A 个人主义、B 现实主义、D 现代主义都是社会思潮名词，不能与 risk-taking 并列，也无法“随幸福而来”。
定位同句 would 5 the way companies invested：宾语是 the way，能与“方式”搭配的是 change（改变投资方式）。A miss、C spoil（破坏）语义过偏且不接 the way，B echo 意为“附和、重复”，与“探究幸福感是否影响投资方式”的研究目的相反。
定位第四段②句 compared U.S. cities' average happiness 6 by Gallup polling：过去分词作后置定语，盖洛普民调对幸福度做的是“测量”，measured 与 compared 一起构成数据来源。A imagined、C assumed、D invented 都指主观虚构，与“民调”这一客观手段矛盾。

定位第四段首句 7 enough, firms' investment and R&D intensity were correlated with the happiness of the area：研究者正想验证这一关联，结果“果然”如此，Sure enough 是固定表达。B 若要表“奇怪的是”须用 Oddly enough，选项缺 -ly；C 同理缺 -ly；D Often 不与 enough 连用。
定位 the happiness of the area in which they were 8：they 指上文 publicly traded firms，公司“总部设在”某地，be headquartered in 为固定说法。A divided（被分割）、B advertised（被宣传）、C overtaxed（被课重税）都无法表达“所在地”这层意思。
定位 or could something else about happier cities 9 why firms there spend more on R&D：why 从句需要一个能带原因宾语的动词，explain why 意为“解释为何”。A summarize、B overstate（夸大）、D emphasize 只能接名词性宾语，无法引出原因从句。
定位 the researchers controlled for various 10 that might make firms more likely to invest，破折号后 like size, industry, and sales 正是这些“因素”。B stages（阶段）、C levels（水平）、D methods（方法）都涵盖不了规模、行业、销售额这三项并列内容。
定位 and for indicators that a place was 11 to live in, like growth in wages or population：工资与人口增长是“宜居”的标志，desirable 意为“值得向往的、宜居的”。B sociable 形容人“好交际”，C reliable、D reputable 多用于人或机构，都不修饰地点。

定位 The link between happiness and investment generally 12 even after accounting for these things：控制变量后关联依然“成立、保持”，hold 作不及物动词正表此意。A resumed（恢复）暗示曾经中断，D broke 与“关联仍存在”相反，B emerged 强调“显现”，与 generally 的稳定语气不合。
定位 younger firms, which the authors 13 to "less codified decision making process"：attribute A to B 意为“把 A 归因于 B”，即作者把年轻企业相关性更强归因于决策程序不规范。A assign（分派）、C transfer（转移）、D compare（比较）都不能与 to 搭配出“归因”之义。
定位 younger and less 14 managers who are more likely to be influenced by sentiment：less 与 younger 并列，说明管理者“更年轻、经验更少”，故填 experienced。A serious、B civilized、C ambitious 既不能与 younger 构成递进，也解释不了“易受情绪影响”。
定位 The relationship was 15 stronger in places where happiness was spread more 16：前句已说年轻企业中关联更强，此处再补一层“也同样更强”，also 表递进追加。A instead 表替代，D never 表否定，B thus 表因果，都读不出“再添一条证据”的语气。

定位 where happiness was spread more 16，下句 where most people are relatively happy, rather than in places with happiness inequality 正是对本空的解释：幸福感分布“更均匀”。A rapidly 讲速度，B directly、C regularly 都不对应“人人相对快乐”这一分布状态。
定位 17 this doesn't prove that happiness causes firms to invest more..., the authors believe it at least...：前句让步、主句转折，While 意为“虽然”。B Until、C After 是时间关系，D Since 是原因或时间，都读不出“承认局限、仍下结论”的让步语气。
定位 the authors believe it at least 18 at that possibility：作者措辞谨慎，只说数据“暗示”这种可能，hint at 意为“暗示”。A arrives at 表“得出（结论）”，语气过强；B jumps at（急于接受）、D strikes at（打击）与学术表述的克制不符。
定位 local culture and sentiment would help 19 how executives think about the future：文化氛围“塑造”高管的思维方式，shape 与 how...think 搭配自然。A share（分享）、B rediscover（重新发现）、C simplify（简化）都表达不出这种潜移默化的影响。

定位 happy people would be more forward-thinking and creative and 20 R&D more than the average：与 forward-thinking、creative 并列，说快乐的人“更倾向于”投入研发，lean towards 意为“倾向于”。A pray for（祈求）、C send out（发出）、D give away（赠送）都与研发投入无关。

sections.title: Text 1　编程课的价值不在写代码
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：编程课不为造程序员，而在训练思维、适应数字生活。21 题对应 thought processes。

paras.en: It's true that high-school coding classes aren't essential for learning computer science in college. Students without experience can catch up after a few introductory courses, said Tom Cortina, the assistant dean at Carnegie Mellon's School of Computer Science.
paras.zh: 诚然，高中编程课对于在大学学习计算机科学并非必需。卡内基梅隆大学计算机科学学院副院长汤姆·科尔蒂纳说，没有相关经验的学生上几门入门课就能赶上。

paras.en: However, Cortina said, early exposure is beneficial. When younger kids learn computer science, they learn that it's not just a confusing, endless string of letters and numbers — but a tool to build apps, or create artwork, or test hypotheses. It's not as hard for them to transform their thought processes as it is for older students. Breaking down problems into bite-sized chunks and using code to solve them becomes normal. Giving more children this training could increase the number of people interested in the field and help fill the jobs gap, Cortina said.
paras.zh: 然而科尔蒂纳说，早接触是有益的。年幼的孩子学计算机科学时，会明白它不只是一串令人困惑、没完没了的字母和数字，而是能用来开发应用、创作艺术品或验证假设的工具。对他们来说，转变思维过程不像对年龄更大的学生那样难。把问题拆成小块、再用代码去解决，会成为习以为常的做法。科尔蒂纳说，让更多孩子接受这种训练，可以增加对这一领域感兴趣的人数，有助于填补岗位缺口。

paras.en: Students also benefit from learning something about coding before they get to college, where introductory computer-science classes are packed to the brim, which can drive the less-experienced or -determined students away.
paras.zh: 在上大学之前就接触一些编程，对学生也有好处——大学里的计算机入门课挤得满满当当，这会把经验不足或决心不够的学生挤走。

paras.en: The Flatiron School, where people pay to learn programming, started as one of the many coding bootcamps that's become popular for adults looking for a career change. The high-schoolers get the same curriculum, but "we try to gear lessons toward things they're interested in," said Victoria Friedman, an instructor. For instance, one of the apps the students are developing suggests movies based on your mood.
paras.zh: 熨斗学校是人们付费学编程的地方，最初只是众多编程训练营之一，这类训练营在寻求转行的成年人中颇受欢迎。高中生上的是同样的课程，但“我们会尽量把课往他们感兴趣的东西上引”，该校教师维多利亚·弗里德曼说。例如，学生正在开发的一款应用会根据你的心情推荐电影。

paras.en: The students in the Flatiron class probably won't drop out of high school and build the next Facebook. Programming languages have a quick turnover, so the "Ruby on Rails" language they learned may not even be relevant by the time they enter the job market. But the skills they learn — how to think logically through a problem and organize the results — apply to any coding language, said Deborah Seehorn, an education consultant for the state of North Carolina.
paras.zh: 熨斗学校的学生大概不会中途退学去打造下一个 Facebook。编程语言更新换代很快，他们学的“Ruby on Rails”到进入就业市场时可能已经用不上了。但他们学到的技能——如何有逻辑地思考一个问题并整理结果——适用于任何编程语言，北卡罗来纳州教育顾问德博拉·西霍恩说。

paras.en: Indeed, the Flatiron students might not go into IT at all. But creating a future army of coders is not the sole purpose of the classes. These kids are going to be surrounded by computers — in their pockets, in their offices, in their homes — for the rest of their lives. The younger they learn how computers think, how to coax the machine into producing what they want — the earlier they learn that they have the power to do that — the better.
paras.zh: 的确，熨斗学校的学生也许根本不会进入 IT 行业。但培养未来的程序员大军并不是这些课程的唯一目的。这些孩子今后一生都将被计算机包围——口袋里的、办公室里的、家里的。他们越早了解计算机如何思考、如何哄着机器产出自己想要的东西——越早知道自己有这样的能力——就越好。

items.stem: Cortina holds that early exposure to computer science makes it easier to
items.exp: 定位第二段③句 It's not as hard for them to transform their thought processes as it is for older students：早年接触让“转变思维过程”更容易，remodel the way of thinking 是其同义改写。A 借末段 job market 设套，C 把 test hypotheses 挪成“提出假设”，D 把 create artwork 夸成“完善艺术创作”。

items.stem: In delivering lessons for high-schoolers, Flatiron has considered their
items.exp: 定位第四段②句 we try to gear lessons toward things they're interested in：课程围绕“他们感兴趣的东西”来设计，即考虑兴趣。A 与第三段“经验不足者被挤走”相反，C 是成人转行者关心的事，D 的学业背景文中未提。

items.stem: Deborah Seehorn believes that the skills learned at Flatiron will
opts: help students learn other computer languages
have to be upgraded when new technologies come
need improving when students look for jobs
enable students to make big quick money
items.exp: 定位第五段末句 the skills they learn ... apply to any coding language：技能可迁移到任何编程语言，即有助于学其他语言。B 把 languages have a quick turnover 误读成“技能要升级”，C 与 apply to any coding language 相反，D 的“快速赚大钱”文中完全没有依据。

items.stem: According to the last paragraph, Flatiron students are expected to
opts: stay longer in the information technology industry
become better prepared for the digitalized world
compete with a future army of programmers
items.exp: 定位末段③④句 These kids are going to be surrounded by computers ... The younger they learn how computers think ... the better：孩子未来生活在计算机环绕的环境中，越早懂原理越有利，即“为数字化世界做好准备”。A 与“不必然入行 IT”相悖，B、D 都把末段读成“长期从业”“与程序员竞争”。

items.stem: The word "coax" (Line 4, Para. 6) is closest in meaning to
items.exp: 定位末段④句 how to coax the machine into producing what they want：coax 本义“哄劝”，此处指设法让机器产出想要的结果，与 persuade（劝诱、说服）最接近。B frighten（吓唬）、C misguide（误导）、D challenge（挑战）都带对抗或强制色彩，与 coax 的“顺着来”相反。

sections.title: Text 2　松鸡保护的“降级”交易
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：为换取州政府与地主合作，松鸡只列“受威胁”而非“濒危”。27 题落在 regulatory power。

paras.en: Biologists estimate that as many as 2 million lesser prairie chickens — a kind of bird living on stretching grasslands — once lent red to the often grey landscape of the midwestern and southwestern United States. But just some 22,000 birds remain today, occupying about 16% of the species' historic range.
paras.zh: 生物学家估计，多达 200 万只小草原松鸡——一种生活在连绵草原上的鸟——曾为美国中西部和西南部常常灰暗的景色添上一抹红色。但如今仅存约 2.2 万只，约占该物种历史分布范围的 16%。

paras.en: The crash was a major reason the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) decided to formally list the bird as threatened. "The lesser prairie chicken is in a desperate situation," said USFWS Director Daniel Ashe. Some environmentalists, however, were disappointed. They had pushed the agency to designate the bird as "endangered," a status that gives federal officials greater regulatory power to crack down on threats. But Ashe and others argued that the "threatened" tag gave the federal government flexibility to try out new, potentially less confrontational conservation approaches. In particular, they called for forging closer collaborations with western state governments, which are often uneasy with federal action, and with the private landowners who control an estimated 95% of the prairie chicken's habitat.
paras.zh: 数量暴跌是美国鱼类及野生动植物管理局（USFWS）决定正式将该鸟列为“受威胁”物种的主要原因。“小草原松鸡处境危急，”USFWS 局长丹尼尔·阿什说。然而一些环保人士感到失望。他们曾力促该机构把这种鸟定为“濒危”，这一级别赋予联邦官员更大的监管权，以打击各种威胁。但阿什等人认为，“受威胁”的标签让联邦政府有灵活空间去尝试新的、可能对抗性更小的保护方式。他们尤其呼吁与西部各州政府以及私人土地所有者建立更紧密的合作——前者常对联邦的干预感到不安，后者控制着约 95% 的松鸡栖息地。

paras.en: Under the plan, for example, the agency said it would not prosecute landowners or businesses that unintentionally kill, harm, or disturb the bird, as long as they had signed a range-wide management plan to restore prairie chicken habitat. Negotiated by USFWS and the states, the plan requires individuals and businesses that damage habitat as part of their operations to pay into a fund to replace every acre destroyed with 2 new acres of suitable habitat. The fund will also be used to compensate landowners who set aside habitat. USFWS also set an interim goal of restoring prairie chicken populations to an annual average of 67,000 birds over the next 10 years. And it gives the Western Association of Fish and Wildlife Agencies (WAFWA), a coalition of state agencies, the job of monitoring progress. Overall, the idea is to let "states remain in the driver's seat for managing the species," Ashe said.
paras.zh: 例如，根据该计划，只要土地所有者或企业签署了覆盖整个分布区的栖息地恢复管理计划，该机构表示就不会起诉那些无意中杀死、伤害或惊扰这种鸟的人。该计划由 USFWS 与各州协商达成，要求因经营而破坏栖息地的个人和企业向一项基金缴款，以每毁掉一英亩就补上两英亩适宜栖息地的方式加以替代。该基金还将用于补偿留出栖息地的土地所有者。USFWS 还设定了一个中期目标：在未来 10 年内使松鸡数量恢复到年均 6.7 万只。它并把监测进展的工作交给西部鱼类及野生动植物机构协会（WAFWA）——一个由各州机构组成的联盟。阿什说，总体思路是让“各州继续坐在管理该物种的驾驶座上”。

paras.en: Not everyone buys the win-win rhetoric. Some Congress members are trying to block the plan, and at least a dozen industry groups, four states, and three environmental groups are challenging it in federal court. Not surprisingly, industry groups and states generally argue it goes too far; environmentalists say it doesn't go far enough. "The federal government is giving responsibility for managing the bird to the same industries that are pushing it to extinction," says biologist Jay Lininger.
paras.zh: 并非人人都买这套双赢说辞。一些国会议员正试图阻止该计划，至少十余个行业团体、四个州和三个环保团体正在联邦法院提出质疑。不出所料，行业团体和各州普遍认为它走得太远，环保人士则说它走得还不够远。“联邦政府把管理这种鸟的责任，交给了那些正把它推向灭绝的行业，”生物学家杰伊·利宁格说。

items.stem: The major reason for listing the lesser prairie chicken as threatened is
opts: the underestimate of the grassland acreage
a desperate appeal from some biologists
items.exp: 定位第二段首句 The crash was a major reason ... decided to formally list the bird as threatened，而 The crash 即首段 just some 22,000 birds remain today、仅占历史分布 16% 的数量暴跌，A 正是它的同义改写。B 的草地面积无据，C 把“处境危急”的引语当成生物学家的呼吁，D 与地主控制栖息地的事实相反。

items.stem: The "threatened" tag disappointed some environmentalists in that it
opts: was a give-in to governmental pressure
would involve fewer agencies in action
items.exp: 定位第二段④⑤句 They had pushed the agency to designate the bird as "endangered," a status that gives federal officials greater regulatory power：他们要“濒危”是因为那给联邦更大监管权，最终只给了“受威胁”，等于监管权更小。A 把“州政府不满联邦干预”说成“向政府压力让步”，B 的机构数量、D 的“违背保护政策”均无据。

items.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 3 that unintentional harm-doers will not be prosecuted if they
opts: agree to pay a sum for compensation
volunteer to set up an equally big habitat
offer to support the WAFWA monitoring job
promise to raise funds for USFWS operations
items.exp: 定位第三段①②句：免于起诉的条件是签署栖息地恢复计划，而该计划要求破坏栖息地的个人和企业 pay into a fund，为每毁一英亩补两块新地，即出钱补偿。B 把“缴款由基金统一补地”说成“自己另建同等大小栖息地”，且原文是 2 acres 并非 equally big；C 混淆 WAFWA 的监测职责，D 的“为 USFWS 筹钱”也非基金用途。

items.stem: According to Ashe, the leading role in managing the species is
items.exp: 定位第三段末句 the idea is to let "states remain in the driver's seat for managing the species," Ashe said：driver's seat 即主导地位，主语是 states。A 与“联邦退居协调”相反，B 的 wildlife agencies 只承担监测进展，C 的地主是被豁免和被补偿的一方。

items.stem: Jay Lininger would most likely support
items.exp: 定位末段末句利宁格的话：联邦把管理权交给“正把该物种推向灭绝的行业”，可见他与环保主义者立场一致。A 的行业团体、D 的受质疑计划正是他批评的对象，B 的双赢说辞是他开篇就否定的，三者都站到了他的对立面。

sections.title: Text 3　读书时间不是挤出来的
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：深度阅读要的是“特殊时间”，靠固定安排而非挤碎片。34 题 default state 指阅读。

paras.en: That everyone's too busy these days is a cliche. But one specific complaint is made especially mournfully: There's never any time to read.
paras.zh: 如今人人都太忙，这是老生常谈。但有一样具体的抱怨说得格外悲切：从来没有时间读书。

paras.en: What makes the problem thornier is that the usual time-management techniques don't seem sufficient. The web's full of articles offering tips on making time to read: "Give up TV" or "Carry a book with you at all times." But in my experience, using such methods to free up the odd 30 minutes doesn't work. Sit down to read and the flywheel of work-related thoughts keeps spinning - or else you're so exhausted that a challenging book's the last thing you need. The modern mind, Tim Parks, a novelist and critic, writes, "is overwhelmingly inclined toward communication… It is not simply that one is interrupted; it is that one is actually inclined to interruption." Deep reading requires not just time, but a special kind of time which can't be obtained merely by becoming more efficient.
paras.zh: 使问题更难办的是，通常的时间管理技巧似乎并不管用。网上满是教人挤时间读书的文章：“戒掉电视”，或者“随身带一本书”。但依我的经验，用这类办法腾出零碎的三十分钟并不奏效。坐下来读书，与工作有关的思绪就像飞轮一样转个不停——要么你已疲惫不堪，一本有难度的书恰恰是你最不需要的。小说家兼评论家蒂姆·帕克斯写道，现代人的头脑“压倒性地倾向于交流……问题不只是人被打断，而是人本身就倾向于被打断”。深度阅读需要的不仅是时间，而是一种特殊的时间，这种时间无法仅靠提高效率获得。

paras.en: In fact, "becoming more efficient" is part of the problem. Thinking of time as a resource to be maximised means you approach it instrumentally, judging any given moment as well spent only in so far as it advances progress toward some goal. Immersive reading, by contrast, depends on being willing to risk inefficiency, goallessness, even time-wasting. Try to slot it in as a to-do list item and you'll manage only goal-focused reading — useful, sometimes, but not the most fulfilling kind. "The future comes at us like empty bottles along an unstoppable and nearly infinite conveyor belt," writes Gary Eberle in his book Sacred Time, and "we feel a pressure to fill these different-sized bottles (days, hours, minutes) as they pass, for if they get by without being filled, we will have wasted them." No mind-set could be worse for losing yourself in a book.
paras.zh: 事实上，“提高效率”本身就是问题的一部分。把时间视为一种应被最大化的资源，意味着你以工具化的态度对待它，只把某一刻判断为“过得值”，且仅限于它推进了向某个目标的进展。相比之下，沉浸式阅读取决于是否愿意冒低效、无目标、甚至浪费时间的风险。试着把它当作待办清单上的一项塞进去，你只能得到目标导向的阅读——有时有用，但不是最令人满足的那种。“未来像空瓶子一样，沿着一条停不下来、几乎无限的传送带向我们涌来，”加里·埃伯利在《神圣时间》一书中写道，“当这些大小不一的瓶子（天、小时、分钟）经过时，我们感到一种要把它们填满的压力，因为若它们空着过去，我们就浪费了它们。”再没有比这更不利于让自己沉浸在一本书里的心态了。

paras.en: So what does work? Perhaps surprisingly, scheduling regular times for reading. You'd think this might fuel the efficiency mind-set, but in fact, Eberle notes, such ritualistic behaviour helps us "step outside time's flow" into "soul time." You could limit distractions by reading only physical books, or on single-purpose e-readers. "Carry a book with you at all times" can actually work, too — providing you dip in often enough, so that reading becomes the default state from which you temporarily surface to take care of business, before dropping back down. On a really good day, it no longer feels as if you're "making time to read," but just reading, and making time for everything else.
paras.zh: 那么什么才管用？也许出人意料：为阅读安排固定的时间。你会以为这可能会助长“效率至上”的心态，但事实上，埃伯利指出，这种仪式化的做法帮助我们“走出时间的洪流”，进入“灵魂时间”。你可以只读纸质书，或用单一功能的电子阅读器，以此减少干扰。“随身带一本书”其实也管用——前提是你足够频繁地沉浸其中，使阅读成为默认状态，你只是暂时浮出水面处理事务，然后重新沉回去。在真正美好的一天里，你不再觉得是在“挤时间读书”，而只是在读书，并为其他一切挤出时间。

items.stem: The usual time-management techniques don't work because
opts: what they can offer does not ease the modern mind
what challenging books demand is repetitive reading
what people often forget is carrying a book with them
what deep reading requires cannot be guaranteed
items.exp: 定位第二段末句 Deep reading requires ... a special kind of time which can't be obtained merely by becoming more efficient：深度阅读要的是效率手段给不了的“特殊时间”，与 cannot be guaranteed 对应。A 把“现代人易被打断”当成全部原因，它只是文中一层；B 的 repetitive reading 无据；C 是文中已被否定的建议。

items.stem: The "empty bottles" metaphor illustrates that people feel a pressure to
items.exp: 定位第三段⑤句 we feel a pressure to fill these different-sized bottles (days, hours, minutes) as they pass：空瓶喻指一段段时间，人怕它们空着过去而急于填满，即让流逝的时间“充实”。A 把 to-do list 当成目的，C 的“完成计划”是另一层含义，D 的 carefree reading 与“带着压力填满”正相反。

items.stem: Eberle would agree that scheduling regular times for reading helps
items.exp: 定位第四段②③句：固定时间阅读看似 fuel the efficiency mind-set，实则 such ritualistic behaviour helps us "step outside time's flow" into "soul time"，soul time 正对应第三段的 immersive reading。A 与 but in fact 的转折相反，B 的线上阅读习惯无据，C 只是把 ritualistic 换个说法，属同义反复而非落点。

items.stem: "Carry a book with you at all times" can work if
opts: reading becomes your primary business of the day
all the daily business has been promptly dealt with
you are able to drop back to business after reading
time can be evenly split for reading and business
items.exp: 定位第四段⑤句 providing you dip in often enough, so that reading becomes the default state from which you temporarily surface to take care of business：阅读是“默认状态”，工作只是临时浮出水面，即阅读成为当天的首要之事。B 把“暂时处理事务”读成“事务全部办完”，C 把方向颠倒成“读完书回到工作”，D 的“平均分配”与主次分明矛盾。

items.stem: The best title for this text could be
opts: How to Find Time to Read
items.exp: 定位首段末句 There's never any time to read 提出问题，二、三段分析常规时间管理为何失灵，末段给出“固定时间阅读”的解法，通篇围绕“如何找到读书时间”。A 的 easy reading 与文中 deep/immersive reading 相反，C 的设定目标恰是作者批评的 goal-focused 做法，D 只涉及阅读广度。

sections.title: Text 4　成功终点相同，路径不同
sections.dir: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
sections.note: 主线：两代人要同样的里程碑，但年轻人路径不同且起步更难。37 题别被“育儿”项带偏。

paras.en: Against a backdrop of drastic changes in economy and population structure, younger Americans are drawing a new 21st-century road map to success, a latest poll has found.
paras.zh: 一项最新民调发现，在经济与人口结构剧烈变化的背景下，较年轻的美国人正在绘制一张 21 世纪通往成功的新路线图。

paras.en: Across generational lines, Americans continue to prize many of the same traditional milestones of a successful life, including getting married, having children, owning a home, and retiring in their sixties. But while young and old mostly agree on what constitutes the finish line of a fulfilling life, they offer strikingly different paths for reaching it.
paras.zh: 跨越代际，美国人仍然珍视许多相同的人生成功传统里程碑，包括结婚、生子、拥有住房，以及在六十多岁时退休。但尽管年轻人和年长者在“什么算圆满人生的终点线”上大体一致，他们通往终点的路径却截然不同。

paras.en: Young people who are still getting started in life were more likely than older adults to prioritize personal fulfillment in their work, to believe they will advance their careers most by regularly changing jobs, to favor communities with more public services and a faster pace of life, to agree that couples should be financially secure before getting married or having children, and to maintain that children are best served by two parents working outside the home, the survey found.
paras.zh: 调查发现，与年长者相比，人生刚刚起步的年轻人更可能把工作中的个人成就感放在首位，更相信经常跳槽最能推进事业发展，更喜欢公共服务更多、生活节奏更快的社区，更认同情侣在结婚或生育前应有经济保障，并更坚持认为孩子最好由双方父母都外出工作来养育。

paras.en: From career to community and family, these contrasts suggest that in the aftermath of the searing Great Recession, those just starting out in life are defining priorities and expectations that will increasingly spread through virtually all aspects of American life, from consumer preferences to housing patterns to politics.
paras.zh: 从职业到社区再到家庭，这些反差表明，在剧烈的大衰退之后，那些人生刚刚起步的人正在界定一些优先事项与期望，它们将日益渗透到美国人生活的几乎方方面面，从消费偏好到居住模式再到政治。

paras.en: Young and old converge on one key point: Overwhelming majorities of both groups said they believe it is harder for young people today to get started in life than it was for earlier generations. While younger people are somewhat more optimistic than their elders about the prospects for those starting out today, big majorities in both groups believe those "just getting started in life" face a tougher climb than earlier generations in reaching such signpost achievements as securing a good-paying job, starting a family, managing debt, and finding affordable housing.
paras.zh: 年轻人和年长者在一个关键点上看法一致：两个群体中的绝大多数人都说，他们认为今天的年轻人起步比前几代人更难。虽然年轻人对今天起步者的前景比年长者略为乐观，但两个群体中的大多数人都认为，那些“人生刚刚起步”的人在取得诸如找到一份高薪工作、组建家庭、管理债务、找到负担得起的住房这些标志性成就方面，面临比前几代人更艰难的攀登。

paras.en: Pete Schneider considers the climb tougher today. Schneider, a 27-year-old auto technician from the Chicago suburbs, says he struggled to find a job after graduating from college. Even now that he is working steadily, he said, "I can't afford to pay my monthly mortgage payments on my own, so I have to rent rooms out to people to make that happen." Looking back, he is struck that his parents could provide a comfortable life for their children even though neither had completed college when he was young. "I still grew up in an upper middle-class home with parents who didn't have college degrees," Schneider said. "I don't think people are capable of that anymore."
paras.zh: 皮特·施奈德认为今天的攀登更难。这位来自芝加哥郊区、27 岁的汽车技师说，大学毕业后他费了很大劲才找到工作。即便现在工作稳定，他说：“我无力独自偿还每月的房贷，只能把房间租出去才应付得来。”回望过去，令他感慨的是，父母当年虽然没有一个人读完大学，却能给子女提供舒适的生活。“我在一个中上阶层家庭长大，父母都没有大学文凭，”施奈德说，“我觉得现在的人已经做不到这样了。”

items.stem: One cross-generation mark of a successful life is
items.exp: 定位第二段①句 Americans continue to prize many of the same traditional milestones ... including getting married, having children, owning a home, and retiring in their sixties：跨代公认的成功标志包含结婚生子。A 的“不同生活方式”正是两代分歧所在，C 与“六十多岁退休”相反，D 的创业盈利文中未提。

items.stem: It can be learned from Paragraph 3 that young people tend to
opts: give priority to childcare outside the home
items.exp: 定位第三段长句 to agree that couples should be financially secure before getting married or having children：年轻人认同婚前、生育前须有经济保障，即重视婚前财务。A 与 a faster pace of life 相反，B 与 regularly changing jobs 相反，D 把“双亲都外出工作”曲解为“优先选择家庭外托育”。

items.stem: The priorities and expectations defined by the young will
opts: reach almost all aspects of American life
items.exp: 定位第四段：priorities and expectations that will increasingly spread through virtually all aspects of American life，即“几乎波及美国生活的方方面面”。A 的 clear 讲清晰度，B 的“物质化”属主观评判，C 把“从消费偏好到政治”的举例误读为“取决于政治偏好”。

items.stem: Both young and old agree that
opts: the old made more life achievements
housing loans today are easy to obtain
getting established is harder for the young
items.exp: 定位第五段①句 Overwhelming majorities of both groups said ... it is harder for young people today to get started in life：老少共识是“年轻人起步更难”，getting established 正是其同义替换。A 只是后者列举的一项，B 的“老一辈成就更多”文中无比较，C 与“找负担得起的住房”之难相反。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about Schneider?
opts: He found a dream job after graduating from college.
His parents believe working steadily is a must for success.
His parents' good life has little to do with a college degree.
He thinks his job as a technician quite challenging.
items.exp: 定位末段④句 his parents could provide a comfortable life for their children even though neither had completed college：父母没有大学文凭却过上中产生活，说明好生活与文凭关系不大。A 与 struggled to find a job 相反，B 把“他工作稳定”说成父母的成功观，D 把 considers the climb tougher 曲解成“技术工作有挑战”。

sections.title: Section II Part B　小标题匹配（七选五）
sections.dir: Read the following text and answer the questions by choosing the most suitable subheading from the list A-G for each of the numbered paragraphs (41-45). There are two extra subheadings which you do not need to use. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
sections.note: 五个段落各提一条“向孩子学快乐”的建议。43 题 Be silly 与 44 题 Have fun 最易混。
sections.intro:
Act Your Shoe Size, Not Your Age

As adults, it seems that we are constantly pursuing happiness, often with mixed results. Yet children appear to have it down to an art — and for the most part they don't need self-help books or therapy. Instead, they look after their wellbeing instinctively, and usually more effectively than we do as grownups. Perhaps it's time to learn a few lessons from them.

blocks.en: What does a child do when he's sad? He cries. When he's angry? He shouts. Scared? Probably a bit of both. As we grow up, we learn to control our emotions so they are manageable and don't dictate our behaviours, which is in many ways a good thing. But too often we take this process too far and end up suppressing emotions, especially negative ones. That's about as effective as brushing dirt under a carpet and can even make us ill. What we need to do is find a way to acknowledge and express what we feel appropriately, and then — again, like children - move on.
blocks.zh: 孩子难过时会怎样？他会哭。生气时呢？他会喊。害怕时？大概两者兼有。随着长大，我们学会控制情绪，使情绪可控、不支配我们的行为，这在许多方面是好事。但我们常常把这一过程做得过头，最终压抑情绪，尤其是负面情绪。那效果无异于把灰尘扫到地毯下面，甚至可能让我们生病。我们要做的是找到一种方式，恰当地承认并表达自己的感受，然后——同样像孩子那样——继续前行。
blocks.exp: 定位段末 What we need to do is find a way to acknowledge and express what we feel appropriately：全段从孩子哭、喊写起，落到“成年人别压抑情绪，要恰当表达”，故 Express your emotions。C 的 Ask for help 只借“需要”一类字眼设置，段内并无求助之意，是最强的动作词干扰。

blocks.en: A couple of Christmases ago, my youngest stepdaughter, who was nine years old at the time, got a Superman T-shirt for Christmas. It cost less than a fiver but she was overjoyed, and couldn't stop talking about it. Too often we believe that a new job, bigger house or better car will be the magic silver bullet that will allow us to finally be content, but the reality is these things have very little lasting impact on our happiness levels. Instead, being grateful for small things every day is a much better way to improve wellbeing.
blocks.zh: 几个圣诞节前，我最小的继女（当时九岁）收到一件超人 T 恤作圣诞礼物。它花了不到五英镑，她却欣喜若狂，说个不停。我们常常以为，一份新工作、更大的房子或更好的车会是那颗神奇银弹，能让我们终于心满意足；但现实是，这些东西对我们幸福水平的持久影响微乎其微。相反，每天为小事心怀感激，才是提升幸福感的更好办法。
blocks.exp: 定位段末 being grateful for small things every day is a much better way to improve wellbeing：五英镑的 T 恤就让九岁孩子欣喜若狂，作者借此说“为小事感恩、容易满足”。E 的 Don't overthink it 讲的是别过度追求幸福，与“小物件带来大快乐”不是一回事。

blocks.en: Have you ever noticed how much children laugh? If we adults could indulge in a bit of silliness and giggling, we would reduce the stress hormones in our bodies, increase good hormones like endorphins, improve blood flow to our hearts and even have a greater chance of fighting off infection. All of which would, of course, have a positive effect on our happiness levels.
blocks.zh: 你可曾注意到孩子们笑得多吗？如果我们大人也能纵情犯点傻、咯咯笑一阵，就能减少体内的压力激素，增加内啡肽这类有益激素，改善心脏的血液流动，甚至更有可能抵御感染。所有这些当然都会对我们的幸福水平产生积极影响。
blocks.exp: 定位首二句 Have you ever noticed how much children laugh? If we adults could indulge in a bit of silliness and giggling：作者劝大人也去“犯傻、咯咯笑”，故 Be silly。B 的 Have fun 过于笼统，且与 44 段的“安排时间享受”撞车；G 的 Notice things 只是借首句 noticed 一词，句意重心并不在“观察”。

blocks.en: The problem with being a grownup is that there's an awful lot of serious stuff to deal with — work, mortgage payments, figuring out what to cook for dinner. But as adults we also have the luxury of being able to control our own diaries and it's important that we schedule in time to enjoy the things we love. Those things might be social, sporting, creative or completely random (dancing around the living room, anyone?) - it doesn't matter, so long as they're enjoyable, and not likely to have negative side effects, such as drinking too much alcohol or going on a wild spending spree if you're on a tight budget.
blocks.zh: 做成年人的麻烦在于，有太多严肃的事要应付——工作、房贷、想晚饭做什么。但作为成年人，我们也有能掌控自己日程的奢侈，重要的是要安排出时间享受我们喜爱的事。这些事可以是社交的、体育的、创作的，或者完全不靠谱的（在客厅里跳舞，有人来吗？）——都没关系，只要它们令人愉快，且不太可能产生负面影响，比如酗酒，或者在预算紧张时疯狂购物。
blocks.exp: 定位第二句 it's important that we schedule in time to enjoy the things we love：成年人能掌控日程，所以应留出时间“享受所爱之事”，故 Have fun。C 的 Ask for help 只因段首提到工作、房贷等琐事而被联想出来，段内通篇在讲“玩乐与放松”，从未提及求助。

blocks.en: Having said all of the above, it's important to add that we shouldn't try too hard to be happy. Scientists tell us this can backfire and actually have a negative impact on our wellbeing. As the Chinese philosopher Chuang Tzu is reported to have said: "Happiness is the absence of striving for happiness." And in that, once more, we need to look to the example of our children, to whom happiness is not a goal but a natural byproduct of the way they live.
blocks.zh: 说了上面这些，还必须补充一点：我们不该太用力地去追求幸福。科学家告诉我们，这可能会适得其反，实际上对我们的身心有害。正如传说中中国哲学家庄子所说：“幸福就是不追求幸福。”在这一点上，我们再一次需要以孩子为榜样——对他们来说，幸福不是一个目标，而是他们生活方式的自然副产品。
blocks.exp: 定位首句 we shouldn't try too hard to be happy，并以庄子“幸福就是不追求幸福”收束：作者反对把幸福当目标死磕，即别想太多、别用力过猛，故 Don't overthink it。G 的 Notice things 在本段毫无落点，只是主题词的泛化干扰；A、B 讲的是具体做法，与本段的“克制”基调不符。

sections.title: Section III　翻译
sections.dir: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 难点：the longer...the more 三级递进要顺着译；rationally selective 即“理性挑选”。

paras.en: The supermarket is designed to lure customers into spending as much time as possible within its doors. The reason for this is simple: The longer you stay in the store, the more stuff you'll see, and the more stuff you see, the more you'll buy. And supermarkets contain a lot of stuff. The average supermarket, according to the Food Marketing Institute, carries some 44,000 different items, and many carry tens of thousands more. The sheer volume of available choice is enough to send shoppers into a state of information overload. According to brain-scan experiments, the demands of so much decision-making quickly become too much for us. After about 40 minutes of shopping, most people stop struggling to be rationally selective, and instead begin shopping emotionally — which is the point at which we accumulate the 50 percent of stuff in our cart that we never intended buying.
paras.zh: 超市的设计目的，就是诱使顾客在店里待尽可能长的时间。原因很简单：你在店里待得越久，看到的东西就越多；看到的东西越多，买得就越多。而超市里的东西实在很多。据食品营销协会的数据，一家普通超市拥有约 4.4 万种不同商品，许多超市还要多上数万种。可供选择的种类之浩繁，足以让购物者陷入信息过载的状态。脑部扫描实验表明，如此繁多的决策需求很快就会让我们不堪重负。购物约 40 分钟后，大多数人便不再努力保持理性挑选，转而开始凭情绪购物——而此时，我们的购物车里已经堆上了 50% 本没打算买的东西。

words: 纯粹的数量，数量之庞大

sections.title: Section IV Part A　应用文（书信·回复祝贺并给建议）
sections.dir: Suppose you won a translation contest and your friend, Jack, wrote an email to congratulate you and ask for advice on translation. Write him a reply to 1) thank him, and 2) give your advice. You should write about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET. Do not use your own name. Use "Li Ming" instead. Do not write your address. (10 points)
sections.note: 两个要点各占一半：谢要谢到“比赛+来信”，建议要落到实处，署名固定 Li Ming。
sections.sample:
Dear Jack,

Thank you so much for your kind words on my winning the translation contest. Your congratulations mean a lot to me, and I am glad to hear that you are also interested in translation.

As for your question, I would like to offer three suggestions. First, read widely in both languages, for a good translator must first be a good reader. Second, practise regularly: translate one short passage every day and compare your version with a published one. Third, do not translate word for word; try to convey the meaning in natural Chinese.

I hope these tips are of some help. Write to me if you have more questions.

Yours,
Li Ming
tips: 格式先立住：称呼 Dear Jack，正文先致谢再给建议，结尾 Yours, Li Ming；不写地址，也不用真实姓名
两点都要落实且分量相当：感谢要具体到“夺冠”与“来信祝贺”，建议要可操作，落到多读、勤练、意译优先
用 First / Second / Third 分层，既清楚又能撑起 100 词；少写 I am very happy 之类的空话，多给具体做法

sections.title: Section IV Part B　图表作文
sections.dir: Write an essay based on the chart below. In your writing, you should 1) interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. You should write about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
sections.note: 饼图：欣赏风景 37% 与缓解压力 33% 合计七成，先说主导两项，再合并说其余三项。
sections.sample:
The pie chart shows the purposes of travel among students of a certain university. Appreciating scenery accounts for the largest share at 37 percent, followed by relieving stress at 33 percent, while making friends and cultivating independence take up 9 percent and 6 percent respectively, and the remaining 15 percent goes to other reasons.

Two features deserve attention. First, the two leading items add up to 70 percent, which means travel is mainly valued as a way to relax and to enjoy natural beauty rather than to gain practical skills. Second, the small proportion of independence and friendship indicates that students still regard travel chiefly as a personal escape instead of social training.

In my view, this trend is understandable, since college life is full of pressure from study and job hunting. Yet students might benefit more if they consciously use trips to meet new people and to solve problems on their own, so that travelling becomes both a rest and a lesson in growing up.
tips: 第一段只读数：37% 与 33% 要先合并成“七成”，再点出 9%、6% 与 15%，五项平铺会显得没有重点
第二段做归纳：两项主导说明旅游被当作“放松＋看风景”，小额项说明“社交与独立”仍非主要动机
第三段评价给一句两面：减压可以理解，但可主动借旅行练社交与独立，落到“旅游既是休息也是成长”
